prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” roofing company for every Miami hurricane-rated replacement — the right contractor depends on your roof type, budget, building code requirements (Miami‑Dade High Velocity Hurricane Zone rules), and whether they can install systems with a Miami‑Dade NOA (Notice of Acceptance). Instead of one name, pick a contractor that meets a clear set of hurricane‑specific qualifications.

How to choose the best contractor for hurricane‑rated replacement
- Miami‑Dade NOA experience: They must routinely install products/systems listed for Miami‑Dade HVHZ (NOA). Ask which NOA numbers they use for your system.  
- Proper licensing and insurance: Florida State Certified Roofing Contractor (or local county license), current general liability and workers’ comp. Verify licenses at myfloridalicense.com.  
- Manufacturer certifications: Approved/authorized installer for the product you want (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, DECRA, Duro‑Last, etc.).  
- Code knowledge and permitting: Will pull permits and follow Florida Building Code and Miami‑Dade installation requirements (nail patterns, uplift calculations, secondary barriers).  
- Proven hurricane details: installation of hurricane straps/ties, secondary water barrier (peel‑and‑stick), impact‑resistant materials where required, correct deck attachment and fasteners.  
- Warranties: Manufacturer warranty + written workmanship/installation warranty. Understand what’s transferable and what’s prorated.  
- References & local track record: Request recent local jobs, ask for photos, and check BBB, Google reviews, and any complaints filed with Miami‑Dade or the state.  
- Transparent contract: Fixed scope, materials specified (brand/model/NOA), start/finish dates, payment schedule, and permit/inspection responsibilities.

Questions to ask every contractor
- “Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide proof?”  
- “Which Miami‑Dade NOA covers this roof system, and can I see it?”  
- “Do you pull permits and coordinate inspections?”  
- “Who will handle insurance paperwork if I’m filing a claim?” (avoid contractors who insist on assignments of benefits)  
- “What are the exact materials and warranty terms?”  
- “Can you show recent local examples of similar jobs and provide references?”

Red flags
- No license or insurance documents, insists on cash-only, pressures you to sign immediately, extremely low bids with vague scope, wants Assignment of Benefits (AOB) for insurance claims without explanation.

Types of systems usually chosen for hurricane resistance
- Impact‑rated architectural shingles (Class 4) installed per HVHZ specs  
- Metal roofing panels (standing seam, through‑fastened with correct clips where approved)  
- Adhered or mechanically attached tile systems approved with NOA  
- Commercial membranes (TPO, PVC, EPDM, Duro‑Last) with proper edge anchorage and seams

What I can do next
- If you give your address or a short list of companies you’re considering, I can help vet them (what to check on their license/NOA, sample questions tailored to each bid, and a side‑by‑side comparison checklist).  
- If you want, I can provide a downloadable checklist or sample contract language to use when getting bids.

If you’d like company names, tell me whether you want national firms or local Miami contractors and I’ll provide a short vetted list plus pros/cons and what to verify for each.
